overall_assessment: No personal data is left in any of the 12 courses, nor in a scan of all 249 NLA plans (no e-mails, phone numbers, staff names, approval stamps or semester-year labels). Every pre-pass flag is a false alarm caused by reference content in the truncated reading lists: a date inside a vatican.va URL (phone), publication dates such as 'Vårt Land 19. januar 1994' (admin_date), and Boal/Levinas named in a reference title (name_like). The one systematic defect is the em-dash academic year 'Studieår: 2019 — 2020', left in every NLA plan; the time regex also strips film running times from two KRLE reading lists.

findings.description: Every NLA plan keeps the academic year in its header block, written with an em-dash ('Studieår: 2024 — 2025', '2025 — 2026', and so on). The rubric says academic years must be removed. The year is in all 12 packet courses and in all 249 NLA offerings (8 distinct values, 2017 — 2018 to 2025 — 2026). It is not personal data, but it is administrative dating in the published course_plan. Deduplication is not affected, because normalize_plan_text() strips all 4-digit years before hashing. The pre-pass ADMIN_DATE_RX has no academic-year pattern, so it does not flag these (admin_date count 4 instead of 249).
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(): the academic-year rule `\b\d{4}\s?[-–]\s?\d{2,4}\b` (line 310) and .drop_academic_year() (line 261) only accept '-' and '–' (en dash). NLA's page writes U+2014 EM DASH ('2017 — 2018', codepoints 32 8212 32), so nothing matches. NLA has no institution handler.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the em dash to the dash class in both places: `\b\d{4}\s?[-–—]\s?\d{2,4}\b` in .anon_generic() and `(\d{4})\s?[-–—]\s?(\d{2,4})` in .drop_academic_year(). Consecutive-year ranges ('2019 — 2020') are then dropped, and content ranges ('1945 — 1970') stay. Add a test in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R: anonymize_text('nla', 'Studieår:\n2019 — 2020') leaves no year, and 'perioden 1945 — 1970' is unchanged. Optionally add `\b\d{4}\s?[-–—/]\s?\d{2,4}\b` (consecutive years) to ADMIN_DATE_RX in R/audit/prepare_anonymization.R so the pre-pass sees this. Then run tar_make() and read metrics_check: all 249 NLA plans shrink by about 11 characters.

findings.evidence: FILMER: A Monster Calls (2016). Lengde: [−2:19−] Om å være og ha (2002).
findings.description: The generic time rule removes film running times from the reading list (FILMER section): 'Lengde: 2:19', '1:45', '2:07' and '2:04' all go. These are course content (the films' length counts towards the syllabus workload, '= ca 1625 sider'), not timestamps. What is left is a dangling 'Lengde:' with no value ('The Passion of the Christ. Lengde: Klassen (2008).'). This is the known failure mode of an over-eager H:MM pattern. In the packet it affects 2 of 12 courses, both suspects; across all 249 NLA offerings, only these 2 KRLE201A offerings have H:MM strings.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic() line 315: `\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?\b` removes every H:MM, whatever its context.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip durations: add a bounded negative lookbehind for duration labels, e.g. `(?<!(?i:lengde|varighet|spilletid|length|duration):?\s)\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?\b`. Or, more generally, remove H:MM only in timetable contexts (after 'kl.', in a range 'HH:MM–HH:MM', or after a date). Add a test that 'Lengde: 2:19' is kept and 'kl. 10:15' is removed.
